title: The nose and smell
examples: Does my nose get stuffy if I have a cold?
Can I really taste things with just my nose?
Why do smells make me remember things?

explain.say: The nose has tiny parts called smell receptors.
These receptors are like tiny detectors for smells.
When you smell something, the signal goes to your brain.
Smell and taste work together to help us know what we eat.
For example, smelling fresh bread makes it taste better.
When you eat something strong, like garlic, both senses help you know it.

faq.q: Why does food taste different when I have a cold?
faq.a: A cold can stuff up your nose, which blocks the smell receptors. If you cannot smell well, the food will taste duller.
asks: Why do I lose my sense of smell when sick?
Does a blocked nose change my taste?

faq.q: Are my taste buds in my tongue only for taste?
faq.a: No, your sense of taste is greatly improved by your sense of smell. They work as a team.
asks: Is smell more important than taste?
How do smell and taste connect?

faq.q: Can I smell things with my mouth?
faq.a: No, you smell things using your nose. Your mouth is for tasting and speaking.
asks: Do I use my tongue to smell?
Where does the smell signal go?

faq.q: Do I need to eat food that smells strong?
faq.a: No, you need to eat a balanced diet. Strong smells are just one way your body uses these senses.
asks: Is it good to smell spices?
What is the purpose of smell receptors?

faq.q: Does my sense of smell get better as I get older?
faq.a: Sometimes, the sense of smell can change as we age. Keeping our noses clean helps keep them working well.
asks: Can I train my sense of smell?

facts: The receptors are located inside the nose.
Taste buds detect basic tastes like sweet and sour.
Smell receptors detect thousands of different scents.
The brain combines signals from both senses for flavor.

quiz.say: If your nose is blocked, your food will taste:
quiz.why: Because smell helps make food taste its best.

wrong.0: This is wrong because a blockage usually reduces the sense of smell.
wrong.2: This is wrong because smell does not change the basic taste.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the tongue detects sourness, not the nose.

quiz.say: What detects the basic tastes like sweet and sour?
quiz.why: Taste buds are located on your tongue to detect basic tastes.

wrong.0: Nerve endings carry the signal, but the taste buds are the detectors.
wrong.2: Smell receptors are in the nose, not on the tongue.
wrong.3: The brain interprets the signals, but it does not detect the taste itself.

quiz.say: Which sense is most important for knowing the full flavor of food?
quiz.why: Flavor is a combination of what you smell and what you taste.

wrong.1: This is wrong because food smells add a lot to the flavor.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the tongue detects the basic tastes.
wrong.3: The eyes help you see food, but they do not create flavor.
